notes.note: Reviewed terminal session, gateway, channel, journal and process-census boundaries plus executable mutation ownership. Unknown tty names cause census refusal before signals; the adapter retains owned-handle kill and reports failure. Pending exact-address/global budgets, bounded HTTP replay and socket backlog pause remain local personal-operator behavior. Shared HTTP/HTTPS protocols preserve replay filtering; seven prior applicable survivor regressions are now caught and the redundant session paused check is removed. Fixture/real local PTY proof remains separate from hosted, Windows, native and remote qualification.

Reviewed current b1 authority, custody, admission and replay claims. Concrete ttysN/pts/N census names fail closed; 9th same-address pending auth is refused, four IPv4 addresses or four IPv6 siblings fill the global budget, and a raw peer ignoring close is terminated promptly after the auth deadline. Fixed-address timeout failures do back off at ten failures; early disconnect releases a slot without a failure (source inspection), so renewal remains possible. This local-only availability gap is accepted, not remote/relay fairness qualification. Two stored 40 KiB records exercise incomplete-page refusal independently of byte count, an empty-reset route fixture returns 200, and a wire barrier proves data pauses then resumes. Every changed behavior has a caught fault and green exact restoration.

Reviewed terminal HTTP and socket admission/error claims, Project binding authority, constructor retention and POSIX cleanup limits. HTTP replay refuses a partial page even when returned payload is only 40 KiB and permits a record-free retention reset. Both HTTP and socket filters use the same HTTP/HTTPS allowlist. Unknown tty census refuses group signaling, kills the owned shell handle and reports cleanup failure. Existing API shapes and prose remain accurate; no live pairing, account, relay or device qualification is added.

No origin, credential or device/Project authorization is widened. Exact source-address pending limits remain vulnerable to multi-address exhaustion and shared-address lockout; this accepted loopback/LAN tranche gap is explicitly disclosed in the owning terminal design, not promoted to remote availability protection.
